text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred in February 20 in history.
1653 - The Dutch fleet under Van Tromp was defeated by the English at the battle of Portland.
1707 - Aurangzeb, last of the great Mughal Emperors of India, died. Under his rule, the Mughal Empire reached its furthest extent.
1790 - Joseph II, Holy Roman Emperor, died and was succeeded by Leopold II of Austria.
1809 - After rejecting Joseph as King of Spain, the city of Zaragoza finally fell to the French under Lannes after a prolonged siege.
1811 - Austria declared itself bankrupt.
1864 - In the American Civil War, the Confederates under General Joseph Finnegan beat Federal forces at the battle of Ocean Pond.
1888 - Marie Rambert, founder of Britain's oldest ballet company, born in Warsaw.
1904 - Alexei Kosygin, Soviet Prime Minister from 1964-1980, born. He tried to co-exist with the West and made state visits to France and Britain to demonstrate his intentions.
1920 - Robert Peary, U.S. Arctic explorer, died. He was credited as the first man to reach the North Pole in 1909.
1924 - Sydney Poitier, the first black actor to win an Oscar, born. Best known for "In the Heat of the Night" and "Guess Who's Coming to Dinner".
1925 - Robert Altman, U.S. film director, born. Best known for his films "M*A*S*H", "Nashville" and "The Player".
1938 - British Foreign Minister Anthony Eden resigned in protest at Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain's policy of appeasement.
1942 - The Japanese invaded Portuguese Timor and Portugal protested to Japan.
1947 - Lord Louis Mountbatten was named as the last Viceroy of India.
1962 - John Glenn became the first U.S. astronaut in Earth's orbit when the Mercury capsule Friendship VII launched him into space.
1966 - Chester William Nimitz, U.S. admiral, died. During World War Two he commanded the Pacific fleet.
1979 - 175 people were killed by an eruption of the Sinira volcano in Indonesia.
1984 - Harris Shoerats, the oldest man in Britain, died aged 111.
1985 - The sale of contraceptives was made legal in Ireland.

1990 - Soviet Parliamentary leaders proposed a draft law which would allow the republics the right to break away from the Soviet Union. The law provided for any secession proposal to be decided by a referendum.
1994 - Yemen's rival leaders, Ali Abdullah Saleh and Vice-President Ali Salem Al Baidh, signed a pact designed to end more than six months of feuding.
1996 - Two senior Iraqi defectors and their families crossed into Iraq six months after fleeing the other way. They were pardoned by Saddam Hussein.
